text:
DONE. JobRef is now (jobId, arrayIndex) — cluster is gone from operational identity entirely.

This completes what A1 could only work around. A1 introduced JobKey to match on the fields that actually identify a job while JobRef still carried a cluster; with the field removed, JobKey became redundant and was DELETED — JobRef is the key. All the conflict machinery A1 needed (clusterConflictsWith, the observation-cluster-conflict and accounting-cluster-conflict diagnostics, the paired Unavailable branches) is gone too, because there is no longer a cluster for a report to disagree about. ControlTransition's observation and accounting paths are materially simpler than before A1.

THE POLICY DECISION, and it is the interesting part: the two surfaces that report a cluster mean opposite things, and now get opposite treatment.

- `sbatch --parsable` appends `;cluster` ONLY on a federated submission. That is now REFUSED with diagnostic code federation-unsupported. Accepting the id while discarding the cluster would mint a JobRef that addresses the wrong cluster on every later query and cancellation — silently. Refusing is the honest response to a site this version cannot address.
- `squeue` reports the local cluster name on every row, federated or not. That is retained as EVIDENCE on JobObservation.reportedCluster and never touches attribution. Treating it as federation would break every ordinary site.

Getting these two backwards in either direction is a real defect, which is why the distinction is stated in docs/compatibility.md alongside the rest of the policy: -M/--clusters is emitted nowhere, and genuine scoped identity waits until grouping, CLI routing, parser attribution, persistence and cancellation can land together.

Wire change: JobRef loses its cluster field. Two golden fixtures re-pinned. Note SchedulerCapabilities.cluster is UNTOUCHED and still reports the site's cluster — that is capability evidence, not job identity, and my first fixture edit nearly removed it by pattern-matching the key name alone.

Tests rewritten rather than deleted, in both directions: ClusterAttributionSuite now asserts an observation reporting a cluster is applied AND keeps it as evidence; AttributionLawSuite's cluster-conflict properties were replaced by properties on what identity now is (array elements are distinct identities; an element is never its parent; a reported cluster cannot reach identity by any route). SlurmParsersSuite's "retains the optional cluster" test became a federation-refusal test plus a single-cluster parse test.

Verification: full suite 417 green on Scala 3.3.8 AND 3.8.4, zero warnings under -Werror, scalafmt clean.
